summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to over INR5 billion and EBITDA margin hit 32%; FY28 guidance of $400M revenue and $160M EBITDA reaffirmed.
summary.overview: Management reported a third consecutive quarter of sequential growth, with revenue up 37% YoY and 15% QoQ to over INR5 billion. EBITDA grew 53% YoY and 32% QoQ, with margin expanding more than 400 bps QoQ to 32%, and H1 EBITDA up 47% YoY. Growth was attributed to the second DDC cartridge line, which began commercial batches in September after a roughly six-month delay, doubling total sterile production days. Management reaffirmed FY28 guidance of $400M revenue and $160M EBITDA, while flagging that the third line may only partly contribute in Q4 FY27 and commercialisation could slip to early FY28.

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in absolute terms; margin 32%
financial_highlights.change: EBITDA +53% YoY, +32% QoQ; margin up more than 400 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.value: About $350k marginal FX impact in Q2
Current (low) ETR to continue until at least Q3 FY28

segments.name: DDC (drug-device combination, cartridge/pen filling)
segments.commentary: Line 2 (500-litre batches) operational since September 2026, doubling sterile production days; Line 1 runs at roughly 50,000-55,000 pens/day, with Line 2 implied at 120,000-130,000. MSA/CSA mix expected to reach 75:25 commercial to MSA at steady state.

segments.name: Biologics
segments.commentary: Won 2 end-to-end projects from a US biotech and an additional programme from a top animal health company, following EU wins last quarter. RFP funnel described as the highest ever; all guidance-period biologics revenue expected to be MSA (pre-approval R&D), with commercial revenue from FY29.

segments.name: Base business (injectables and softgels)
segments.commentary: Injectables and softgels both grew in Q2 with multiple launches. Injectable site shutdown began late September and runs through Q3, with new prefilled syringe and lyophilisation capacity from January. Softgel capacity increased about 3x over the past year, with 80%+ visibility on utilisation; a greenfield softgel site is planned.

guidance_outlook: FY28 guidance reaffirmed: $400M revenue and $160M EBITDA (reported basis, per management).
Management expects H2 FY27 to be stronger than H1.
Third DDC line passed FAT in Germany and is on site for qualification; start targeted for Q4 FY27 but commercialisation may slip to start of FY28; all three lines expected fully operational for FY28.
Dr. Reddy's semaglutide API supply has commenced, with supplies to start within the current quarter; Canadian supply ramp from other customers on track for Q3.
Debt to remain under 1.5x EBITDA; ROCE expected in high-20s by end FY28; company expects to move towards free cash generation.
Working-capital delays from geopolitics add 45-60 days to cycle times, seen as temporary and expected to normalise within 1-2 quarters.
capex_capacity: DDC Line 2 (500-litre batches) running commercial batches since September 2026; target sterile days of 225-230 per year at steady state. Line capability up to 750 litres.
DDC Line 3 completed FAT in Germany and is at site awaiting qualification; qualification involves multiple European vendors.
Injectables site planned shutdown began late September 2026, continuing through Q3; new prefilled syringe and lyophilisation capacity available from January 2027.
Softgel capacity increased ~3x over the last year at the current site, which cannot expand further; a greenfield softgel site is planned, adding high-potent and containment capability.
Unit 2 (flagship site) headcount to rise 2x-3x in FY27 to support capacity build-out.
demand_pricing: Semaglutide India volumes rose from 20,000-25,000 units/month before patent expiry (Feb) to over 200,000 units/month by September.
Canada semaglutide market grew from 8M to 12M units and is now about 16-17M units post genericisation; management sees Canada and Brazil at 4-6x current levels over time.
Hikma launched first generic semaglutide in Saudi Arabia; company holds all four Canadian approvals; Brazil approvals pending for many customers.
Pricing is volume-based rather than market-based; management says no major realisation shift expected into FY28, with batch-size efficiency gains shared with customers.
Management says geopolitics added 2-3 pp P&L pressure across the industry, but pass-through raw materials limited the impact on OneSource's P&L.

qa_highlights.question: What is softgel capacity utilisation and when will the new DDC line reach optimum utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Cartridge line ramp expected to be quick given demand; softgel utilisation rising with 80%+ visibility, but the current site is full, hence the greenfield plan.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q4 FY27 exit run-rate of about $90M and 36-38% margin be consistent with FY28 $400M guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a Q4 exit run-rate; reiterated FY28 guidance and that all three lines will be available in FY28, with Q4 partial availability dependent on qualification.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables rose in H1 FY27 - is this a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to geopolitical shipping and container delays adding 45-60 days to cycle times; viewed as timing, not structural, with no quality issue in receivables.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ETR outlook and how long will the deferred tax benefit last?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ETR expected to continue at least until Q3 FY28, as brought-forward losses are utilised.

qa_highlights.question: How long for a new line to ramp from 10-15% to 70-80% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Qualification of bespoke lines takes significant time, but utilisation ramps quickly once started; target 225-230 sterile days a year, with Line 3 expected to follow the same pattern.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE and deleveraging plan beyond EBITDA margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt to stay under 1.5x EBITDA; ROCE expected high-20s by end FY28; free cash generation to follow the investment cycle.

risks_watch: Line 3 qualification timing: commercialisation may slip into early FY28, which could back-end DDC contribution and pressure the FY28 guidance.
Working-capital strain: receivables up in H1 FY27 due to 45-60 day delivery delays; management expects normalisation within 1-2 quarters.
Dr. Reddy's supply recovery and Canadian semaglutide ramp depend on partner timing and approvals (Brazil, other emerging markets).
Injectables shutdown runs through Q3 FY27; compliance track record must be maintained as new capacity comes online.
Geopolitical shipping and freight costs; management cited a 2-3 pp P&L hit across the industry.
Management declined to split the 12 launches or disclose the MSA/CSA ratio for Q2, and did not give an absolute EBITDA figure, limiting verification.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, biologics funnel and FY28 guidance, but cautious on timing, with repeated caveats that bespoke line qualification may push commercialisation into FY28. Management was evasive on specific molecules, customers, Q4 exit run-rate and beyond-FY28 growth, saying guidance for those will come later.
key_quotes: We expect second half to be stronger than the first. And basis that, we are also reaffirming our FY28 outlook, which we have given of $400 million revenue and $160 million EBITDA.
The delayed deliveries to the customer does impact at least 45 to 60 days in terms of the overall cycle time. I do believe that it is not structural. It is temporary, and it is only a timing impact.
Our pricing to the customers has always been volume-based and not market-based, whether it's emerging markets or Canada or anywhere else, and we don't see that changing.
